newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian army says 300 killed in ethnic violence.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian army says 300 killed in ethnic violence.

text.p: A senior Indonesian army officer has said about 300 people were killed in recent ethnic violence in the province of West Kalimantan on Borneo island, the Media Indonesia newspaper reported on Tuesday.

"It's not true that the number of victims killed reached more than 1,000 like it was quoted in an English-language newspaper in Jakarta. The number of people killed was about 300 people," Major-General Zacky Anwar Makarim, assistant to the army chief of staff for security affairs, was quoted as saying.
The paper gave no further details on the deaths.
A military spokesman was not immediately available to comment on the report.

The military and residents in the province have said at least 12 people died over the past six weeks. However, some residents and church sources say the death toll from the violence, which began in late December and continued until early February, could be much higher.
A report in The Australian newspaper on Tuesday quoted local sources as saying around 600 Madurese have been killed by local Dayaks and dozens of Dayaks had been shot by Indonesian troops.
Makarim was speaking on Monday after Indonesia's army chief blamed outsiders from East Java for outbreaks of ethnic violence in West Kalimantan.
"We have proof, there were bad people from East Java who came there to incite, so something happened which we did not want," General Hartono told reporters at army headquarters in Jakarta on Monday.
He said West Kalimantan, which borders Malaysia's Sarawak state, was peaceful before the arrival of the outsiders from East Java.
"The people were harmonious. After the bad people came, they were restless again," he said, without giving further details.

Ethnic riots broke out in West Kalimantan in late December in what police said was a fight between Dayak and Maduran youths over a girl at a concert in Sanggau Ledo, about 95 km (60 miles) north of Pontianak, the provincial capital.
The fighting between ethnic Dayaks and Madurans, who are migrants from Madura island off East Java, later spread to other parts of West Kalimantan.
Residents say troops still guard several towns even though calm has gradually returned to the province.
